findings.text: non-blocking: the early return added to _remember_count_answer is unreachable from its only caller, because _commits_beyond_base returns the stored count at :402 before it ever computes one and so it is never asked to record a held answer; no test exercises it either, so the second half of the diff carries no behaviour change and would regress silently.

non-blocking: the gate sentence ends 'reads its full sha back out of the two.', a truncated phrase where 'the store' was meant, so the fragment's own account of the assertion is unreadable at the point a later reader checks it.

non-blocking: the matched-arm logs record their revision, tree and command but no partition or scheduler job id, and the sibling arm-baseline.sbatch.log and arm-after.sbatch.log are empty files, so the done_when's 'all_debug partition job ... never on the fleet node' clause cannot be confirmed from the run's own artefacts.

item_verdicts.call_sites: verified the two production writers' callers: reckon/crew/recovery_review_subject.py:337 (_resolve_commit, uncached on the tick path) and reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:420 (_commits_beyond_base).
item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit against base 5617397173: f5e5e8e52d adds the two early returns and the 98-line test, 041192e26d adds the 34-line evidence fragment; no other file changes.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when names tests/test_a_steady_tick_writes_no_known_answer.py resolving 20 citations twice on a temporary crew home; the file asserts 20 writes then 0 writes with st_ino and st_mtime_ns unchanged across the second pass (:71, :82, :83), and gate-head.log records '2 passed in 9.60s' EXIT=0.
item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is 'skip rewriting a git answer the store already holds; reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:300 skips the commit-answer write when the store already resolves the candidate to that sha, and :324 adds the same skip to the count-answer writer.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; status complete, commits f5e5e8e52d and 041192e26d, tests the relative gate command, test_logs naming the gate, both arms and the control, baseline_suite and after_suite for the two matched arms; its hygiene line claims 5 pre-existing ruff findings where ruff reports 3, which does not move the delta.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the fence was recovery_watch.py, recovery_review_subject.py, the node's test file, the node's fragment and its figures directory; the diff touches recovery_watch.py, the test file and the fragment, and nothing else.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_steady_tick_writes_no_known_answer.py:82 fails if the skip at recovery_watch.py:300 is reverted, shown by the base-revision control; the count skip added at recovery_watch.py:324 has no assertion and no reachable caller, so it is unguarded.
justifications.evidence: gate-head.log opens at revision f5e5e8e52d with the literal relative command and reads '2 passed in 9.60s' / EXIT=0, and negative-control.log runs the same case at base 5617397173 and fails on 'assert 20 == 0' at test_a_steady_tick_writes_no_known_answer.py:82, which is the declared control.
justifications.fit: reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:292-296 explains the mechanism in the module's own voice beside the pre-existing _stored_commit_answer/_remember_commit_answer pair, and neither the source nor the test carries a plan, section or ticket identifier.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/crew/recovery_watch.py:300 returns before the store's lock when _stored_commit_answer already carries the sha passed in, which is the write the section's profile puts 42.0% of the tick under, and :324 repeats the skip for the count writer.
justifications.reuse: the change extends the store's existing readers (_stored_commit_answer at recovery_watch.py:278, _stored_count_answer at :309) inside their own module, and ruff over a whole-repo search finds no other git answer store to fork.
justifications.scope_discipline: git diff --stat 56173971738a..041192e26d lists recovery_watch.py, the node's test file and the node's evidence fragment, all three inside the four declared write paths; recovery_review_subject.py was fenced and left untouched.
